title: Shadow Evals Telemetry — Metric Dimensions & Cardinality Review (working doc)
content:
Context
- Shadow Traffic ("Shadow Evals") mirrors a sampled subset of live requests to one or more shadow targets and records quality + performance metrics.
- This doc reviews the proposed metric dimensions (tags) and cardinality risks for shadow_eval.* signals.
- Goal: ship useful metrics for Console comparisons + rollout gates without blowing up time series counts, storage, or query latencies.

Owners / reviewers
- Observability: Thomas Baird (owner), Allison Grant (standards)
- Telemetry platform: Logan Wright, Caleb Johnson
- Analytics/cost: Nadia Rahman, Mei Lin
- SRE: Sean Gallagher
- Console backend: Chloe Martin (consumer)

Scope
- Metrics emitted by shadow runner + pipeline aggregation strategy.
- Not covering tracing spans in depth (but notes included where tags should move to traces/logs).

Non-negotiables (from observability standards + SRE feedback)
1) No high-cardinality user/customer identifiers in metrics tags (customer_id, end_user_id, org_id, email, api_key_id).
2) request_id must NOT be a metric tag. Allowed in logs/traces only.
3) Prompt text / tool args / output text must NOT be metric tags.
4) Primary-path latency SLO must be unaffected; shadow metrics collection must not introduce expensive tag computation.

Primary consumers & queries we need to support
A) Console: compare primary vs shadow for a route over time
- Filters: route, environment, region, primary_model_family, shadow_target, (optional) customer_tier
- Breakdowns: success/failure, judge win-rate, latency deltas, cost/token deltas

B) Rollout policies: quality gates
- Evaluate on aggregated metrics (e.g., "judge_win_rate < 0.48 for 10m" or "format_error_rate > 2%")
- Must be stable and resilient to missing data / low sample size

C) SRE: operational health
- Queue depth, drop counts, shadow execution error rates, shadow latency p95/p99


Proposed metric taxonomy (draft)
We will emit two layers:
1) Raw-ish event counters/timers from shadow runner (low tag surface; stable)
2) Aggregated tables (analytics) for deep slicing (route/customer allowlist/etc.)

Layer 1 (metrics)
- Designed for time-series monitoring + alerting.
- Strict tag allowlists, bucketing, and “unknown/other” handling.

Layer 2 (analytics datasets)
- Join shadow_run_event with primary request metadata in warehouse.
- Supports per-customer / per-route drilldowns without impacting metrics cardinality.


Cardinality risk assessment (what’s dangerous)
Potentially explosive dimensions (DO NOT tag on metrics)
- customer_id / org_id / workspace_id (N could be 1000s+)
- route_id if it is effectively unique per customer (also 1000s+)
- request_id (effectively unbounded)
- model_id if it includes commit hashes/build stamps (high churn)
- judge_prompt_version if it includes experiment IDs (moderate churn)
- error_message (unbounded)
- tool_name if user-defined/dynamic (moderate to high)

Dimensions that are usually safe (with constraints)
- region (small set)
- environment (prod/stage)
- shadow_target_id (small if we cap)
- model_family (curated small set)
- quant_profile (small set)
- outcome buckets (ok/error/timeout/dropped)
- status_class (2xx/4xx/5xx)


Recommended global constraints (proposed)
Hard caps / normalization:
- shadow_target_id: max 20 active targets per cluster/region (enforced by config validation); else bucket as "overflow".
- route_key: metrics use route_template_id (platform-generated stable ID) OR route_group (customer-defined but enumerated/validated). No freeform route names.
- model tags: use model_family + model_variant (enum), not raw model_version string. For internal debugging, raw model version belongs in logs.
- judge tags: use judge_family ("rw-judge-v1"), judge_version (semver-like, e.g., "1.2"), not experiment UUIDs.

Missing/invalid tag values
- Any unknown tag value => "unknown" (NOT pass-through).
- Any value failing allowlist => "other" and emit a separate counter shadow_eval.tag_dropped_total{tag="..."}.


Proposed tag allowlists (metrics layer)
NOTE: allowlists are for metrics only. Analytics layer can store richer dims with stricter access control.

Common tags for most shadow_eval.* metrics
- env: ["prod", "staging"]
- region: ["us-east-1", "us-west-2", "eu-west-1"] (expandable; must be platform-managed)
- deployment_mode: ["hosted", "dedicated", "private"] (optional; check if private clusters export to same backend)
- traffic_tier: ["free", "pro", "enterprise"] (derived from billing plan; NOT customer_id)

Route tags (high risk if not controlled)
- route_template_id: platform-generated stable ID, format "rtpl_########" (max ~10k globally; still big, but acceptable if we don’t cross with too many other tags)
- route_group: OPTIONAL customer-configured enum with max 50 values per customer; metrics layer uses only for Redwood-internal dogfooding unless we can enforce global boundedness.

Model/target tags
- primary_model_family: e.g., ["llama", "mistral", "qwen", "mixtral", "rw-embed"] (curated)
- primary_model_variant: e.g., ["8b", "70b", "instruct", "coder", "v2", "v3"] (curated)
- shadow_model_family: same as above
- shadow_model_variant: same as above
- quant_profile: ["fp16", "bf16", "int8", "int4"]
- shadow_target_id: "stgt_########" (platform-generated, stable)

Outcome tags
- result: ["ok", "error", "timeout", "dropped"]
- error_class: ["none", "upstream_4xx", "upstream_5xx", "runner_internal", "queue_full", "budget_exceeded", "judge_error", "redaction_error"]
- http_status_class: ["2xx", "4xx", "5xx"] (for upstream responses)

Judge/safety tags
- judge_family: ["rw-judge-v1"] (maybe also "none")
- judge_version: ["1.0", "1.1", "1.2"] (semver-minor only)
- judge_outcome: ["primary_win", "shadow_win", "tie", "inconclusive", "not_run"]
- safety_outcome: ["pass", "block", "review", "not_run"]

Latency/cost tags
- latency_bucket_ms: ["0_50", "50_100", "100_250", "250_500", "500_1000", "1000_2500", "2500_5000", "5000_plus"] (optional; prefer histograms if backend supports)
- token_bucket: ["0_128", "128_512", "512_2048", "2048_plus"] (only if needed; otherwise store raw numeric as histogram)


Metric-by-metric review (proposed)

1) Operational health (SRE)
- shadow_eval.runner.queue_depth (gauge)
  Tags: env, region
  Notes: no route/model tags.

- shadow_eval.runner.dropped_total (counter)
  Tags: env, region, reason=["queue_full","budget_exceeded","kill_switch","policy_disabled","sampling_zero","invalid_target"]
  Notes: keep reason small.

- shadow_eval.runner.exec_latency_ms (histogram)
  Tags: env, region, result
  Notes: do not split by route/model to avoid time series explosion.

- shadow_eval.runner.exec_errors_total (counter)
  Tags: env, region, error_class

2) Quality metrics (rollout gates / Console comparisons)
We propose *aggregated* quality metrics at (route_template_id, shadow_target_id) granularity, plus a small number of global rollups.

- shadow_eval.judge.win_rate (gauge or derived in query)
  Recommended emission:
  - shadow_eval.judge.verdict_total{judge_outcome=...}
  Tags: env, region, route_template_id, shadow_target_id, judge_family, judge_version
  Cardinality commentary:
  - route_template_id x shadow_target_id is the big multiplier.
  - Mitigation: restrict to 1–2 regions in beta; cap shadow_target_id count; optional: only emit per-route for top-N routes by traffic, others roll up to "route_template_id=other".

- shadow_eval.format_adherence.rate
  Emission:
  - shadow_eval.output.format_total{result=["ok","format_error","not_run"]}
  Tags: env, region, route_template_id, shadow_target_id
  Notes: avoid tagging on schema_name if it’s customer-defined. If we must, bucket schema_name to top-K known schemas + "other".

- shadow_eval.safety.outcome_total
  Tags: env, region, route_template_id, shadow_target_id, safety_outcome

3) Performance deltas (primary vs shadow)
We should avoid tagging deltas by too many dims; keep to route+target only.

- shadow_eval.delta.latency_ms (histogram of (shadow - primary))
  Tags: env, region, route_template_id, shadow_target_id

- shadow_eval.delta.cost_usd_micros (histogram)
  Tags: env, region, route_template_id, shadow_target_id
  Note: cost_usd_micros is computed in telemetry pipeline; shadow runner should only emit raw token counts and model identifiers.


High-cardinality dimensions: where they should live instead
- request_id: traces/logs. Join to metrics via exemplars if supported.
- raw model_version (hash/build id): logs + warehouse, not metrics.
- customer identifiers: warehouse only; Console can show customer-specific views via backend query to aggregated tables with RBAC.
- prompt_hash: warehouse only (possible later; still high cardinality; needs careful gating + retention policy alignment).


Aggregation strategy (recommended)
Why: many customer queries want deep filters. We cannot do all slicing in metrics tags.

A) Emit minimal "shadow_run_event" (structured log/event) from runner
Fields (conceptual; exact schema in Confluence standards):
- ts, env, region
- primary_request_id (for join; not used in metrics)
- route_template_id
- traffic_tier
- primary_model_family/variant, shadow_model_family/variant, quant_profile
- shadow_target_id
- primary_latency_ms, shadow_latency_ms
- primary_input_tokens, primary_output_tokens, shadow_output_tokens
- judge_outcome + judge_version
- safety_outcome
- error_class

B) Telemetry pipeline
- Stage 1: validate/enforce tag allowlists; normalize strings; compute derived buckets.
- Stage 2: write raw events to low-retention store (per Security retention doc; default 7d for payload-free events).
- Stage 3: hourly rollups into aggregate tables:
  - agg_shadow_eval_hourly_route_target
    Dimensions: hour, env, region, route_template_id, shadow_target_id, traffic_tier
    Measures: counts, win_rate numerators/denominators, avg/p50/p95 latency deltas, avg cost delta, safety rates, format_error_rate
  - agg_shadow_eval_hourly_global
    Dimensions: hour, env, region
    Measures: queue health, error rates, global win_rate

C) Console query path
- Prefer querying aggregate tables for route-level comparisons.
- Grafana/alerts use metrics layer for operational health + a small number of quality SLOs.


Proposed “guardrail knobs” (implementation hooks)
- Tag allowlist enforcement at emit-time (SDK helper) + ingest-time (telemetry pipeline). Ingest-time is non-negotiable.
- If the metrics backend rejects series due to explosion, runner should degrade gracefully (drop metric; do not block).
- Backpressure metrics: shadow_eval.telemetry.dropped_tags_total{tag="route_template_id"} etc.


What we should NOT do (explicitly)
- Do not emit one metric series per (customer_id, route_id, shadow_target_id) for GA.
- Do not tag by prompt_config_id if it is not strictly enumerated and bounded.
- Do not add freeform “experiment_name” tags.


Open questions
1) route_template_id cardinality
- How many route templates do we expect across prod at GA? Need data from Console/Routes.
- If >10k, we should add a top-N limiter for per-route emissions and move long-tail routes to analytics-only.

2) Dedicated/Private data-plane differences
- Are all deployments exporting to the same metrics backend? If not, tags like deployment_mode must be stable across pipelines.

3) Judge versioning
- Need a concrete version policy: bump judge_version only on rubric changes that affect win-rate distribution.

4) Safety outcomes
- Confirm consistent meaning of "review" across policies. If per-customer policy differs, we may need to report "blocked" vs "not_blocked" only.


Action items
- [Thomas] Draft final allowlist + publish in Confluence standards page (ties to ENG-2435).
- [Caleb] Add ingest-time enforcement + "tag_dropped" counters in telemetry pipeline.
- [Logan/Nadia] Confirm which fields are needed for cost deltas and where computation occurs.
- [Sean] Validate alertability: which metrics should page (queue depth, runner errors) vs ticket (quality drift).
- [Chloe/Jin Woo] Confirm Console queries can rely on aggregate tables (hourly) and define acceptable freshness (<= 15 min?).

Appendix: quick rule of thumb for series counts
Estimated upper bound (beta):
- regions(3) * env(1-2) * route_template_id(~200 top routes) * shadow_target_id(<=5) * judge_version(<=3)
= 3*2*200*5*3 = 18,000 series for the primary judge metric family (still heavy but manageable if limited to a few metric names).

If we instead allow all routes (~10,000) and targets (~20):
3*2*10,000*20 = 1.2M series (too high). We must keep the product constraints + allowlists aligned.

Notes to self
- Don’t fight the platform reality: deep slicing belongs in warehouse + Console, not in metric tags.
- We should treat “route_template_id x shadow_target_id” as the only large multiplier we allow in metrics, and even that may need top-N gating.
